correctness.rationale: Exhaustive bipartite-partner recursion visits every matching exactly once and a necessary-and-sufficient partner-swap predicate visits all legal alternating squares. Independently, an eighty-edge bitset recursion and eighty-square toggling mechanism give the identical 589185 vertices, 3219360 edges and 120 singleton + 80 four-cycle + 99280 + 489465 component census. Exact union-find connectivity, degree-two certificates for each order-four component, and all 3840 cube automorphisms check the additional assertions. A sign-of-permutation argument proves bipartiteness.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Arbitrary even-cycle flips may connect pairs that square-only flips cannot; a connectedness theorem for the permissive operation does not imply square-only connectivity. General computational-complexity results and \(Q_4\) analyses do not imply an exact \(Q_5\) component census. No decisive stronger prior theorem was identified. In particular, twist invariance and the existence of asymptotically giant components do not determine Q5 component sizes, and connectivity after permitting alternating cycles through length 16 cannot imply connectivity or exact component counts with length 4 only. Fink’s Hamiltonian-union operation is distinct.

value.rationale: A natural fixed-dimension exact classification separates frozen, small cyclic, and two huge noncommunicating sectors of \(Q_5\) perfect matching configurations; this directly diagnoses irreducibility failure of local square-flip sampling.
